title: Synthesize health signals for active-passive multi-region failover and SLO-driven load shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Under partial regional degradations we observe noisy liveness/readiness probe failures and autoscaler oscillation. This leads to unintended cross-region failovers or broad load-shedding that violates SLOs for tail latency and availability. Current probes are evaluated in isolation by region-level controllers and the autoscaler, so transient probe noise causes aggressive scaling or circuit-breaker trips.
objective: Build a health signal synthesizer and control-plane gating that: (1) aggregates probe signals, synthetic transactions, and SLO error-budget state into a single region health score, (2) exposes that score to the autoscaler and routing/circuit-breaker layers, and (3) drives SLO-aware derating/load-shed policies and safe active->passive failover sequencing.
design_decisions: Use a compact health score (0..100) per region synthesized from: readiness fraction, 95th latency delta vs baseline, synthetic transaction failure rate, and error-budget burn rate.
Keep probe adapters local (node/pod-level) to emit time-windowed metrics; aggregator runs in control plane with configurable weightings and hysteresis.

Autoscaler integration: autoscaler consumes health_score and an explicit "derate_factor" signal instead of raw probe counts. Derate_factor instructs autoscaler to reduce target capacity before triggering cross-region failover.

Routing/circuit-breaker integration: routing layer uses health_score thresholds to shift traffic gradually; only trigger active->passive failover when health_score < 20 for >3min and error budget depleted.
Backwards compatibility: default behavior is no-op until feature flag enabled per environment; fall back to current probe-based gating if synthesizer is unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: In simulated partial region outage (disk+network flakiness) staging test, synthesized health_score correctly drops and prevents immediate cross-region failover; observed failover only after graceful thresholds met.
Autoscaler flapping reduced: number of scale operations per 10m window drops by >=70% on noisy probe injection tests.
SLO preservation: customer-facing 99th latency and availability SLOs remain within target with <5% error budget burn during controlled degradation scenarios.
Integration tests and canary rollout completed to two staging clusters and one pilot customer with no regressions in observability dashboards.
Documentation updated: console docs, SDK hooks, and runbooks for on-call are published.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: incorrect weightings could delay necessary failover and violate SLOs. Mitigation: conservative defaults that prefer continued local serving with eskewed routing only after error-budget depletion and manual override.

Risk: control-plane availability could remove health scoring and lead to poor decisions. Mitigation: synthesizer is best-effort; components fall back to raw probe heuristics on synthesizer unavailability.
Risk: added complexity for ops. Mitigation: provide rich explainability metrics and a single health_score timeline in Console with drilldowns per contributor.
Risk: customers with strict compliance may want different thresholds. Mitigation: per-customer override and versioned rollout configs.
